learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of logic (logical statements/ propositions, connectives, arguments, validity of an argument, truth tables and simple circuits)
sla_name: Logic: statements, connectives, arguments, truth tables and circuits
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of logic are explored adequately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Logic is the study of reasoning. It helps to decide whether statements and arguments are true, false or valid.
sla_notes_details: A proposition is a statement that is either true or false. Connectives join propositions: negation (not p), conjunction (p and q), disjunction (p or q), implication (if p then q) and biconditional (p if and only if q). A truth table lists all possible truth values of a compound statement. An argument is valid if the conclusion must be true whenever all its premises are true; a tautology is always true and a contradiction is always false. Logical statements can be represented by simple switching circuits: AND is a series circuit and OR is a parallel circuit.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, p and q is true only when both p and q are true; if p is 'it rains' and q is 'the road is wet', then p implies q is false only when it rains and the road is not wet.
sla_notes_daily_life: Logic is used in computer programming, legal arguments, electrical switching circuits and everyday decision making.
sla_exercise: Construct the truth table for p and q.::TT gives T; TF gives F; FT gives F; FF gives F.||When is p or q false?::Only when both p and q are false.||State the circuit type that represents p and q.::A series circuit.

learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of Algebra (sum and product of roots of a quadratic equation, solve algebraically and graphically simultaneous equations involving one linear and one quadratic equation, use the remainder theorem to find a remainder of a polynomial function of up to third degree)
sla_name: Algebra: quadratic roots, simultaneous equations and the remainder theorem
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of Algebra are explored adequately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: This topic extends algebra to roots of quadratic equations, simultaneous equations of different degrees and polynomial remainders.
sla_notes_details: For ax2 + bx + c = 0 with roots alpha and beta, the sum of roots is -b/a and the product is c/a. A linear and a quadratic equation are solved simultaneously by substituting the linear equation into the quadratic one, and graphically by finding the intersection points of the line and the curve. The remainder theorem states that when a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x - a) the remainder is f(a); if f(a) = 0 then (x - a) is a factor. This is applied to polynomials up to degree three.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, x2 - 5x + 6 = 0 has roots 2 and 3 with sum 5 and product 6. If f(x) = x3 - 2x + 4, dividing by (x - 1) gives remainder f(1) = 3.
sla_notes_daily_life: Such algebra models projectile paths, profit and cost curves and the intersection of supply and demand in business and engineering.
sla_exercise: Find the sum and product of the roots of 2x2 - 6x + 4 = 0.::Sum = 3; product = 2.||Find the remainder when x3 + 2x - 5 is divided by (x - 2).::f(2) = 8 + 4 - 5 = 7.||Solve y = x + 1 and y = x2 - 1 simultaneously.::x = 2, y = 3 or x = -1, y = 0.

learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of Rational Functions (properties, asymptotes, domain and range, graphs)
sla_name: Rational functions: properties, asymptotes, domain, range and graphs
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of Rational Functions are explored appropriately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A rational function is a fraction in which both the numerator and denominator are polynomials.
sla_notes_details: For f(x) = P(x)/Q(x), the domain excludes values that make Q(x) = 0. A vertical asymptote occurs where the denominator is zero and the numerator is not; a horizontal asymptote is found by comparing degrees of the numerator and denominator. Intercepts are found by setting x = 0 and y = 0. The range is the set of values the function can take. To sketch the graph, find intercepts, asymptotes and behaviour near the asymptotes.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, f(x) = 1/(x - 2) has domain all real x except 2, a vertical asymptote x = 2 and a horizontal asymptote y = 0.
sla_notes_daily_life: Rational functions model quantities such as average cost per unit, concentration of a drug and rates in physical systems.
sla_exercise: State the domain of f(x) = 3/(x + 1).::All real numbers except x = -1.||Find the vertical asymptote of f(x) = (x + 2)/(x - 4).::x = 4.||Find the horizontal asymptote of f(x) = 2x/(x + 3).::y = 2.

learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of Differentiation (derivatives of polynomial and trigonometric functions: first principles, power rule, chain rule, product rule and quotient rule)
sla_name: Differentiation of polynomial and trigonometric functions
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of Differentiation are explored adequately.
sla_teaching_aids: Graphing calculators|Differentiation applications|Differentiation games|Mathematical software sucha as GeoGebra
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Differentiation is the process of finding the derivative of a function, which gives its rate of change or the gradient of its graph.
sla_notes_details: From first principles, f'(x) = lim (h to 0) [f(x + h) - f(x)]/h. Rules: the power rule d/dx (xn) = n xn-1; the chain rule dy/dx = dy/du x du/dx; the product rule d(uv)/dx = u dv/dx + v du/dx; the quotient rule d(u/v)/dx = (v du/dx - u dv/dx)/v2. Derivatives of trigonometric functions are d/dx (sin x) = cos x, d/dx (cos x) = -sin x and d/dx (tan x) = sec2 x.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, if y = 3x4 - 5x + 2 then dy/dx = 12x3 - 5, and if y = (2x + 1)3 the chain rule gives dy/dx = 6(2x + 1)2.
sla_notes_daily_life: Derivatives measure speed from distance, marginal cost in economics and the rate of growth in biology.
sla_exercise: Differentiate y = 5x3 - 2x.::dy/dx = 15x2 - 2.||Differentiate y = sin x.::dy/dx = cos x.||Use the product rule to differentiate y = x sin x.::dy/dx = sin x + x cos x.

learning_activity_name: Apply differentiation to determine rates of change of quantities, maxima and minima of functions, turning points, points of inflection and curve sketching
sla_assessment_criteria: Differentiation is appropriately applied to determine rates of change of quantities, relative maximum and minimum of functions, turning points, points of inflection, and curve sketching.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Differentiation is applied to find rates of change, maximum and minimum values and to sketch curves.
sla_notes_details: The rate of change of a quantity is its derivative with respect to time. Stationary (turning) points occur where dy/dx = 0; the second derivative decides the nature: d2y/dx2 > 0 gives a minimum, d2y/dx2 < 0 gives a maximum and a change of sign of d2y/dx2 gives a point of inflection. Curve sketching uses intercepts, turning points, inflection points and behaviour for large x. Optimisation problems find the largest area or the lowest cost.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, for y = x2 - 4x + 3, dy/dx = 2x - 4 = 0 at x = 2, and d2y/dx2 = 2 > 0, so (2, -1) is a minimum point.
sla_notes_daily_life: Businesses find the production level for maximum profit, and engineers design containers using minimum material.
sla_exercise: Find the stationary point of y = x2 - 6x.::dy/dx = 2x - 6 = 0, so x = 3 and y = -9, giving (3, -9).||What does d2y/dx2 < 0 show?::The stationary point is a maximum.||A square's side increases at 2 cm/s. Find the rate of increase of its area when the side is 5 cm.::dA/dt = 2s ds/dt = 2 x 5 x 2 = 20 cm2/s.

sla_name: Indefinite and definite integrals of polynomials and simple trigonometric functions
sla_assessment_criteria: Indefinite and definite integrals of polynomials and simple trigonometric functions are adequately determined.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Integration is the reverse of differentiation and is used to find totals and areas.
sla_notes_details: The indefinite integral of xn is x(n+1)/(n + 1) + c for n not equal to -1, where c is the constant of integration. Also, the integral of cos x is sin x + c and the integral of sin x is -cos x + c. A definite integral has limits a and b: the integral from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is an antiderivative of f, and there is no constant.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, the integral of (3x2 + 2) dx = x3 + 2x + c, and the integral from 1 to 2 of 2x dx = [x2] from 1 to 2 = 4 - 1 = 3.
sla_notes_daily_life: Integration is used to find total distance from a speed function, total cost from a marginal cost function and accumulated quantities in science.
sla_exercise: Integrate 4x3 with respect to x.::x4 + c.||Evaluate the integral from 0 to 3 of 2x dx.::[x2] from 0 to 3 = 9.||Integrate cos x.::sin x + c.

learning_activity_name: Apply Integration to determine area under a curve and volume of a solid of revolution of a simple curve about an axis
sla_name: Integration: area under a curve and volume of revolution
sla_assessment_criteria: Area under a curve and volume of solid of revolution of simple curves about the axes are determined correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Definite integrals give the area between a curve and the x-axis and the volume of solids formed by rotating curves.
sla_notes_details: The area under y = f(x) from x = a to x = b is the integral from a to b of f(x) dx (taking the absolute value where the curve is below the axis). The area between two curves is the integral of the upper function minus the lower function. The volume formed when the curve is rotated about the x-axis through 360 degrees is V = pi times the integral from a to b of y2 dx.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, the area under y = x2 from 0 to 3 is [x3/3] from 0 to 3 = 9 square units, and rotating y = x from 0 to 2 about the x-axis gives V = pi x integral of x2 dx = pi x 8/3.
sla_notes_daily_life: These methods are used to calculate land area, the volume of tanks and other rotational objects such as bottles and pipes.
sla_exercise: Find the area under y = 2x from x = 0 to x = 4.::Integral of 2x = x2, so area = 16 square units.||State the formula for volume of revolution about the x-axis.::V = pi times the integral of y2 dx between the limits.||Why is the absolute value used for area below the x-axis?::Because area cannot be negative.

sla_name: Set theory: three sets, Venn diagrams, cardinality and De Morgan's laws
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of Set Theory are adequately explored.
sla_teaching_aids: Real objects|Set simulations|Charts of different sets|Playing cards|Manila papers|Marker pens|Colored chalks
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Set theory studies collections of objects and the relationships between them.
sla_notes_details: Operations on sets include union, intersection, complement and difference. Venn diagrams with three sets show all possible regions, and the cardinality n(A) is the number of elements of A. For three sets, n(A union B union C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) - n(A and B) - n(B and C) - n(A and C) + n(A and B and C). De Morgan's laws state that (A union B)' = A' intersection B' and (A intersection B)' = A' union B'. Other properties are commutative, associative and distributive laws.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, if n(A) = 10, n(B) = 8, n(A intersection B) = 3 then n(A union B) = 10 + 8 - 3 = 15.
sla_notes_daily_life: Sets are used in classification of data, surveys, database queries and decision making in business.
sla_exercise: State De Morgan's law for (A union B)'.::(A union B)' = A' intersection B'.||If n(A) = 12, n(B) = 9 and n(A union B) = 17, find n(A intersection B).::12 + 9 - 17 = 4.||How many regions are there in a three-set Venn diagram (including outside)?::Eight.

sla_method: Simulations Provide students with various resources such as simulations, graphs and ICT to
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of coordinate geometry are explored appropriately.
sla_teaching_aids: Graph papers|Geometrical models|Shape|Angles animations|Geoboards|AI tools|Mathematical software sucha as Maple|GeoGebra|MATLAB|Mathematica
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Coordinate geometry uses algebra to study points, lines and curves in a plane.
sla_notes_details: The ratio theorem finds a point dividing a line segment AB in ratio m:n: x = (n x1 + m x2)/(m + n), y = (n y1 + m y2)/(m + n). The perpendicular distance from (x1, y1) to the line ax + by + c = 0 is |a x1 + b y1 + c|/sqrt(a2 + b2). The angle between two lines with gradients m1 and m2 is found from tan(theta) = |(m1 - m2)/(1 + m1 m2)|. The equation of a circle with centre (a, b) and radius r is (x - a)2 + (y - b)2 = r2. A locus is the path of a point that moves according to a rule.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, the point dividing A(1, 2) and B(7, 8) in the ratio 1:2 is ((2 x 1 + 1 x 7)/3, (2 x 2 + 1 x 8)/3) = (3, 4).
sla_notes_daily_life: Coordinate geometry is used in surveying, map making, computer graphics and GPS navigation.
sla_exercise: Write the equation of a circle with centre (2, 3) and radius 5.::(x - 2)2 + (y - 3)2 = 25.||Find the distance from (0, 0) to the line 3x + 4y - 10 = 0.::10/5 = 2.||Find the midpoint of (2, 4) and (6, 10).::(4, 7).

sla_name: Trigonometry: identities, double and compound angle formulae and equations
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of trigonometry are explored appropriately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Advanced trigonometry uses identities and formulae to simplify expressions and solve equations.
sla_notes_details: Basic identities: sin2 x + cos2 x = 1, 1 + tan2 x = sec2 x and 1 + cot2 x = cosec2 x. Compound angle formulae: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B, cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B. Double angle formulae: sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A and cos 2A = cos2 A - sin2 A = 1 - 2 sin2 A = 2 cos2 A - 1. Trigonometric equations are solved by using identities to reduce to one function, then finding all solutions within a given interval.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, sin 75 degrees = sin(45 + 30) = sin 45 cos 30 + cos 45 sin 30 = (sqrt(6) + sqrt(2))/4.
sla_notes_daily_life: Trigonometry is used in surveying, navigation, engineering design and wave analysis in physics.
sla_exercise: State the identity relating sin2 x and cos2 x.::sin2 x + cos2 x = 1.||Write sin 2A in terms of A.::2 sin A cos A.||Solve 2 sin x = 1 for 0 to 360 degrees.::x = 30 degrees and 150 degrees.

sla_teaching_aids: Scientific calculators|Mathematical software sucha as Maple|Geogebra|MATLAB|Mathematica|AI tools
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A vector has both magnitude and direction; in three-dimensional space it has three components.
sla_notes_details: A vector is written as ai + bj + ck or (a, b, c). Its magnitude is sqrt(a2 + b2 + c2), and a unit vector is the vector divided by its magnitude. Addition and subtraction are done component by component. The dot product a.b = a1b1 + a2b2 + a3b3 is a scalar, and the cross product a x b is a vector perpendicular to both. The position vector of a point is its vector from the origin.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, for a = 2i + 3j + 6k, |a| = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = 7, so the unit vector is (2i + 3j + 6k)/7.
sla_notes_daily_life: Vectors are used to describe forces, velocity, wind and current, and movement in three-dimensional computer graphics.
sla_exercise: Find |3i + 4j + 12k|.::sqrt(9 + 16 + 144) = 13.||Find (1, 2, 3) + (4, -1, 0).::(5, 1, 3).||Is the dot product a scalar or a vector?::A scalar.

sla_name: Dot product: angle between vectors and work done
sla_assessment_criteria: Dot product of vectors is adequately applied to solve problems involving angle between two vectors and work done by force on an object.
sla_teaching_aids: Vector animations|Mathematical software sucha as GeoGebra|MATLAB
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The dot product connects vectors to angles and to the work done by a force.
sla_notes_details: a.b = |a||b| cos(theta), so cos(theta) = a.b/(|a||b|) gives the angle between two vectors. Two vectors are perpendicular if a.b = 0. The work done by a constant force F moving an object through displacement d is W = F.d.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, for a = (1, 2, 2) and b = (2, 1, 2), a.b = 2 + 2 + 4 = 8, |a| = 3, |b| = 3, so cos(theta) = 8/9 and theta is about 27.3 degrees.
sla_notes_daily_life: Work by forces, such as pulling a load along an inclined path, is calculated using the dot product.
sla_exercise: When are two vectors perpendicular?::When their dot product is zero.||Find (2, 3, 1).(1, 0, 4).::2 + 0 + 4 = 6.||A force (3, 0, 4) N moves an object through (2, 1, 0) m. Find the work done.::W = 6 + 0 + 0 = 6 J.

sla_name: Cross product: normal vectors and area
sla_assessment_criteria: Cross product of vectors is used correctly to find unit vector normal to a given plane and areas of a plane figure.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The cross product of two vectors gives a vector perpendicular to both of them.
sla_notes_details: a x b = (a2b3 - a3b2, a3b1 - a1b3, a1b2 - a2b1) and its magnitude is |a||b| sin(theta). A unit vector normal to the plane containing a and b is (a x b)/|a x b|. The area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b is |a x b|, and the area of a triangle is half of it.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, i x j = k. For a = (1, 0, 0) and b = (0, 2, 0), a x b = (0, 0, 2), so the area of the parallelogram is 2.
sla_notes_daily_life: It is used in engineering and physics to find torque, magnetic force and surface orientation in graphics.
sla_exercise: What is i x j?::k.||Find the area of the triangle with sides (3, 0, 0) and (0, 4, 0).::1/2 x |(0, 0, 12)| = 6.||Is a x b perpendicular to a?::Yes, it is perpendicular to both a and b.

learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of statistics (measures of dispersion: range, variance and standard deviation)
sla_name: Statistics: measures of dispersion (range, variance, standard deviation)
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of statistics are explored appropriately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Measures of dispersion describe how spread out data are around the mean.
sla_notes_details: The range is the largest value minus the smallest. The variance is the mean of the squared deviations from the mean: variance = sum of (x - mean)2/n, and the standard deviation is its square root. A small standard deviation shows data are close to the mean; a large one shows they are more spread out. In business and economics, dispersion measures risk and consistency.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, for the data 2, 4, 6: mean = 4, squared deviations 4, 0, 4, variance = 8/3 and standard deviation is about 1.63.
sla_notes_daily_life: Dispersion is used to compare the consistency of sales, crop yields and exam performance between different groups.
sla_exercise: Find the range of 5, 9, 2, 12.::12 - 2 = 10.||What is the standard deviation in relation to the variance?::It is the square root of the variance.||A larger standard deviation shows what?::The data are more widely spread.

sla_name: Counting techniques: fundamental principle, permutations and combinations
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of counting techniques are explored appropriately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Counting techniques help find the number of ways in which events can occur without listing all of them.
sla_notes_details: The fundamental principle of counting says that if one event can occur in m ways and another in n ways, together they can occur in m x n ways. A permutation is an arrangement in which order matters: nPr = n!/(n - r)!. A combination is a selection in which order does not matter: nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!). The factorial n! = n x (n - 1) x ... x 1, and 0! = 1.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, choosing a president and secretary from 5 students is 5P2 = 20 ways, while choosing a committee of 2 from 5 is 5C2 = 10 ways.
sla_notes_daily_life: Counting methods are used in planning timetables, designing passwords and calculating possible lottery outcomes.
sla_exercise: Calculate 5!.::120.||Find 6C2.::15.||In how many ways can 3 books be arranged on a shelf?::3! = 6.

sla_name: Probability: independent events and conditional probability
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of probability are explored adequately.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Probability measures how likely an event is to occur, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
sla_notes_details: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B). For any events, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). The conditional probability of A given B is P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B). Tree diagrams show the outcomes of successive events.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, the probability of getting two heads when tossing two fair coins is 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4.
sla_notes_daily_life: Probability is used in insurance, weather forecasting, quality control and medical testing.
sla_exercise: If P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5 are independent, find P(A and B).::0.3 x 0.5 = 0.15.||Write the formula for P(A|B).::P(A and B)/P(B).||What is the probability of a certain event?::1.

sla_name: Matrices 3 x 3: operations, determinant and inverse
sla_assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of 3×3 matrices are explored adequately.
sla_teaching_aids: Scientific calculators|Mathematical software sucha as Maple|GeoGebra|MATLAB|AI tools
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A 3 x 3 matrix is a square array of numbers with three rows and three columns.
sla_notes_details: Matrices are added and subtracted element by element, multiplied by a scalar, and multiplied row by column. The determinant of a 3 x 3 matrix is found by expanding along a row or column using cofactors. The inverse exists only if the determinant is not zero: A-1 = (1/det A) x adjoint of A, where the adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, for the identity matrix I, det I = 1 and I-1 = I. If det A = 0 then A has no inverse and is called singular.
sla_notes_daily_life: Matrices are used in computer graphics, economics models, coding and solving many equations at once.
sla_exercise: When does a matrix have an inverse?::When its determinant is not zero.||What is the determinant of the 3 x 3 identity matrix?::1.||Name the matrix used to find an inverse from the cofactors.::The adjoint (transposed cofactor matrix).

learning_activity_name: Use 3×3 matrices to solve systems of linear simultaneous equations with three unknowns
sla_name: Solving systems of three linear equations using matrices
sla_assessment_criteria: 3×3 matrices are used appropriately in solving systems of linear simultaneous equations with three unknowns.
sla_references: TET(2023), ADDITIONAL MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A system of three linear equations with three unknowns can be written as AX = B and solved using matrices.
sla_notes_details: Write the equations as a matrix equation AX = B, where A is the 3 x 3 matrix of coefficients, X the column of unknowns and B the column of constants. If det A is not zero, then X = A-1 B. Alternatively, use row reduction. The solution is checked by substituting into the original equations.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, x + y + z = 6, x - y + z = 2 and x + y - z = 0 form a system that can be solved as X = A-1 B giving x = 1, y = 2 and z = 3.
sla_notes_daily_life: These systems appear in problems about mixtures, budgets, electric circuits and production planning.
sla_exercise: Write the system Ax = B solution formula.::X = A-1 B.||What must be true for the system to have a unique solution?::det A is not zero.||How can you check the solution?::Substitute the values into the original equations.
